title: After a long break the plan week keeps counting, so a 'start lighter' Target also says 'leave only 1 rep in the tank'
what: The followed plan's week is counted only from the calendar, from the day the member started following it. A member who stops for 6 weeks or more comes back many weeks further on, for example 'Week 9 · easy week in week 12', or lands straight in an easy week. For members who log effort, each Target then reads like 'Eight weeks since your last Bench Press. Start a little lighter at 54 kg and build back. This week of your plan, stop each set with about 1 rep left in the tank', which pairs a gentle restart with the hardest week of the block.
expected: After a break of 6 weeks or more the plan's week pauses or restarts its block, so the week line, the effort line and the lighter restart all agree.
who: members who follow a plan and come back after a long break
how_often: every return after 6 weeks or more away
fix_line: Hold the plan's week still during a long break, or restart its block on return

title: The Ask an AI text says a new member trains under once a week
what: The text a member shares with an AI app always divides the workouts by 4 weeks. A member who started 5 days ago and trained 3 times is described as '3 workouts in 4 weeks, about 0.8 a week', and the date range in the same text starts at their first workout, not 4 weeks ago. The AI then advises them to train more often.
expected: The rate is worked out over the days the member has actually been training, or the text says they started on that date.
who: new members using Ask an AI
fix_line: Divide by the weeks since the first workout when that is under 4

items.reason: Phone tracker facts live in the phone's own database, not in Crispy Curves rows, so the comparison was made in code: workouts per month (Profile feed and Statistics use the same count), streak and rest days (Calendar), lifts beating a best this week (Home and finish use one record rule), records per workout (feed card vs finish), last-4-weeks AI text
